lantern_fen_tao.name: Fen Tao
lantern_fen_tao.title: Contracted ordinary relay fitter who retains her own tools

lantern_03_001.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_001.text: On Day 1401, Yue returned to the association records room and found the shutter examiner's stop tag still attached. The affected afternoon window had stayed closed while the admitted morning windows operated under their own inspections. Ma Yan had offered senders their actual alternatives and recorded what each chose. No packet had disappeared from the queue simply because a timetable expected its light. Deng asked Yue to begin with that queue and the charter, rather than a general story about what every relay ought to do.

lantern_03_002.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_002.text: The charter named Alder Reach, Chime Reach, Lower Glass, Moss Ford, Ring Meadow, and East Sill. Each settlement had approved the current service account through its own receiving clerk. Their representatives could request a review but could not sign away other institutions' records. Yue copied the six public names onto a separate scope sheet. The old Azure Cloud households did not appear there. Neither did the valley bell, orchard, archive, or reservoir communities whose work she had encountered. This association was a new body with a specific local boundary.

lantern_03_003.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_003.text: Its relay carried admitted messages between these receiving points. It did not transport a person's body, replace a road, decide title to a house, or certify the truth of every sentence sent through it. The charter's price table separated transmission, handling, and ordinary onward delivery. Ma showed Yue a message whose sender had paid for transmission but omitted the onward cart charge. The message waited at the receiving station with an actual notice sent to its owner. The clerk could not turn the missing service into a free journey by stamping complete.

lantern_03_004.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_004.text: A local gardener wanted the association to deliver a seed order to an unlisted upland hamlet. Deng could quote a contracted ground carrier outside the six points, subject to the hamlet's real receiving arrangement. The gardener wanted the old public lamp emblem to mean every place beneath its light. Yue listened while Deng pointed to the charter. A visible tower could invite that larger interpretation. Its owners still owed people a readable boundary. The gardener chose to ask the carrier's actual price before placing the order.

lantern_03_005.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_005.text: The tower itself stood inside a low walled yard with a public viewing walk outside the isolation rail. Its lower workroom held the fuel cradle, grounded release assembly, packet index, and staffed receiving desks. Yue entered only the public records side with Ma. Jin Lu kept the technical door locked while her examination continued. The keys belonged to appointed operators. A visitor's cultivation cord did not admit her through it, and the proposed documentary work did not require an exception. Yue asked where the admitted equipment description could be read.

lantern_03_006.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_006.text: Ma brought the public maintenance summary to a clear table. It named the old relay's four daily windows and their rated external fuel portions. Detailed calibration pages remained with the licensed examiner, available to a qualified contracted comparison only under its actual permission. Yue could read the public summary now. She made no claim to know the hidden readings. Across the yard, a porter carried a stopped window's packets into the dry queue bay. That ordinary movement had its own count, custodian, and destination while technical work remained unfinished.

lantern_03_007.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_007.text: Deng described the first local appropriation, covering Day 1401 through Day 1445. The association held one thousand and eighty copper under its accepted service minute. Four hundred and twenty was assigned to external fuel purchases; three hundred and sixty to two defined operator supplements; two hundred and ten to contracted ground alternatives; ninety to a proposed source-record appointment. Existing regional base staff and their accepted relief rota had their own annual wage source, shown separately. No one at the table could spend the same copper across those headings.

lantern_03_008.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_008.text: The ninety-copper appointment would buy eighteen calendar days at five copper, with the existing weekly rest and a defined four-hour working period on duty days. It would involve authorised copying and receiving comparisons, not powered operation. Personal food and lodging would remain Yue's own expense unless a later offer named otherwise. Deng showed the proposed dates and asked her to compare them with her accepted basin obligations. The post could start only when its actual duties fitted those obligations; a reserved wage line was not permission to sign her name.

lantern_03_009.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_009.text: Yue asked whether declining the post would cancel Chime's source request. Deng said another qualified copyist could receive the admitted comparison, or the question could wait within its stated review date. Chime had an institution before Yue arrived. It would continue without her. The answer made the offer easier to assess. She wanted the work, but did not want need to become a hidden threat. The minute clerk put the proposed appointment in the pending tray while Yue took a copy to read outside the meeting.

lantern_03_010.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_010.text: In the public yard, a woman was trying to find the queue bay for a delayed message about her son's apprenticeship interview. She had followed an old sign whose arrow pointed through the locked technical door. Ma directed her to the actual desk and gave her a complaint form for the sign. Yue asked permission to record the public arrow's wrong location for the proposed receiving review. The woman agreed to that observation, but declined inclusion of her son's interview fields. Yue wrote the location and left the household matter out.

lantern_03_011.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_011.text: The appointment copy fitted inside Yue's personal notebook without pressing the source wrapper. She took it to the lodging house and calculated living costs. Eighteen days of wages would total ninety. Her current two-copper nightly room and ordinary one-copper meals could use fifty-four across the same period. Thirty-six would remain before postage, clothing, or other purchases. The calculation assumed those actual prices continued and required another plan if they changed. Work that paid a wage could still leave a narrow margin for training she hoped to undertake later.

lantern_03_012.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_012.text: Yue remembered supper on Day 1400, when the lodging keeper confirmed her first six-night renewal after the two arrival nights. It covered Days 1400 through 1405 at two copper nightly. She paid twelve from her existing money while the employment decision remained open. The keeper wanted the association to guarantee another term, but no such guarantee existed. Yue showed her own receipt and said later nights would require actual settled plans. The keeper brought her a clean bowl. She budgeted one copper daily for ordinary food and kept the room payment separate.

lantern_03_013.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_013.text: On Day 1402, Zheng Bao visited the public association desk to request an accessible time for her uncle's future demonstration. He had already declined the coming week's request, and she wanted that refusal retained. Ma found the unaccepted invitation in the proposal tray and marked it declined for those dates. A poster draft still carried Zheng Lin's name. Ma removed it before approval and issued a correction to the person preparing the notice. Bao left after receiving the actual correction copy, with no demand that Yue admire the household's successful boundary.

lantern_03_014.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_014.text: Yue saw Zheng later at his rented rooms under an invitation he had made for the afternoon. He kept the cracked lens on its padded case inside a dry cupboard. Bao's ordinary sewing work occupied the table beside it. She asked Yue not to set wet cups there. Yue used the side stool. Zheng wanted to hear how the charter comparison had gone. She described its public six-settlement scope and proposed duties, leaving other senders' private packets outside the conversation. His own household could be ordinary company without becoming an annex to her work file.

lantern_03_015.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_015.text: Bao earned money repairing winter coats and household covers. Her customers paid for specific work and collected their own garments. One coat lay on the table with a pocket stitched closed by mistake. Bao had found the error before delivery and was reopening it at her own cost. Zheng wanted to help by holding the cloth. She gave him the light task he could do comfortably, then corrected his grip when it pulled the seam. He laughed and asked whether every institution in town had begun inspecting him today.

lantern_03_016.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_016.text: Yue helped turn a finished cover only after Bao offered that task. The cloth smelled faintly of clean starch. Nobody paid her for the visit, and she could leave when she wished. Bao asked whether she had eaten enough since travelling. Yue said she had, though the first local work would need its own living plan. Bao knew a shared room cheaper than the present lodging house. It belonged to a different owner and had its own availability. She supplied an address, not a promise that friendship could manufacture a vacant bed.

lantern_03_017.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_017.text: The cheaper house held a room at one and a half copper per night when booked for an actual eighteen-day term. Its owner wanted payment weekly and supplied no meals. Yue inspected the dry shelf, exit, common washing place, and present room occupants before considering it. The shelf fitted her admitted papers without using somebody else's space. She asked for a written price through the proposed dates. The owner gave it. That quote could reduce her employment living cost, but she had not yet taken the room or cancelled nights already used elsewhere.

lantern_03_018.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_018.text: Deng's clerk had meanwhile compared the proposed duty hours against the remaining basin receiving terms. Any admitted outside consultation would retain a separate time and source record. Yue's local copying could not sign for a basin receiver, and Chime's wages could not purchase an unoffered correction. Deng asked her to bring the actual closing reference to the later review, rather than letting a general description of finished work decide both accounts. Yue accepted that requirement because it named a document she could actually seek and a limit the new institution could keep.

lantern_03_019.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_019.text: Jin Lu completed the shutter check on Day 1403. The worn guide sleeve needed replacement within the assembly's current approved repair scope. She authorised the named ordinary fitter to do it under the isolation plan. The replacement did not renew the oldest joint's remaining life. The stopped afternoon window would stay closed until the post-repair check. Ma gave queued senders the current expected review time and alternatives, then retained their choices on the receiving slate. Yue watched the institution change one operational fact without improving every other part by association.

lantern_03_020.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_020.text: The fitter was a woman named Fen Tao who brought her own inspected tools. She declined the association's unfamiliar spare driver and used the tool whose fit she had checked. Jin received the offered inspection record, not ownership of the driver. Yue could observe from the public safe side but not copy Fen's private working appendix. Fen permitted a public task description after completion. Her price included the stated replacement labour. It did not include teaching every interested visitor how to perform the work.

lantern_03_021.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_021.text: A porter asked Fen to show him the sleeve fitting while she waited for the check. She offered a later training appointment with its own fee and safety conditions. He wanted to avoid the fee because he had already helped move her box. Moving the box was part of his paid association duty; it did not buy her next hour. Ma supported that distinction and gave him the training registry address. Yue heard him complain after Fen closed the technical door. He could dislike the answer without acquiring the demonstration.

lantern_03_022.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_022.text: At the ordinary training registry, Yue asked about Shao Ye's great-circuit curriculum. The registry clerk described a waiting period before preregistration, a prior-certificate review, and separate bench inspection. Shao was working at another admitted examination that morning. The clerk could give Yue a public information sheet and appointment request. It could not announce acceptance in her absence. Yue read the sheet at the outer table. Stage nine required a controlled great circuit through prepared primary routes, with interruptions, recovered trials, and actual next-day tissue checks under registered conditions.

lantern_03_023.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_023.text: She left her current stage certificate closed until the registry named its permitted receiving process. The public sheet supplied no new throughput ceiling and promised no Foundation entry. It described an actual local minimum of eighty-four usable units after the specified work, sampling, sleep, and recovery, with at least ninety-two percent compatibility. Yue compared that minimum with the prior recovered basin readings. The difference would require sustained practice and a body that passed the next checks, not a vigorous declaration beside an application counter.

lantern_03_024.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_024.text: The clerk told her to return on Day 1416 for the preliminary appointment, with the actual tuition and bench provision proposal ready for review. Yue paid the small ordinary application-copy charge from her own money. Its receipt bought the recorded request and copy; it bought no place on the curriculum. She kept the public threshold sheet separate from the certificate she already held. The sheet described a possible next stage. The certificate described work completed under earlier conditions. Neither could stand in for the other simply because both carried an official heading.

lantern_03_025.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_025.text: Back at the association, Ma had corrected the public arrow. The old plank remained stored with the complaint reference because its defect explained the change. The new sign named the actual queue bay and public desk. The apprenticeship sender found it without entering the technical rail. She chose a paid ground carrier for her son's message rather than waiting for the stopped window. The carrier signed the admitted packet count and gave her an expected delivery, with the route's real weather limits. The sign correction had helped her act; it had not delivered the interview answer.

lantern_03_026.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_026.text: Yue wrote one page about the scope comparison for her own pending appointment decision. She wanted the local work because it involved actual people and readable records. She wanted training because the prior reservoir practice had opened a difficult question she could not answer by moving papers. Neither wish entitled her to combine institutional duties until nobody could see their separate limits. She asked Deng for a proposed start date after the current basin timing comparison. Deng agreed to show it at the next accepted sitting, without treating her question as a signature.

lantern_03_027.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_027.text: On Day 1404, the association representatives met in the public hall. Each came under the travel terms their settlement had actually accepted. One representative joined through a signed statement because the household's current care duty prevented a journey. Deng read that statement within its offered public fields. The six places did not gain six physically present bodies by convenience. Their quorum rule admitted the statement for this defined budget sitting, while a different equipment decision would require its own appointed participants. Yue observed from the public bench with permission.

lantern_03_028.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_028.text: Ring Meadow's representative wanted every delayed message charged back to the sender's home point, regardless of where its fault occurred. East Sill's clerk objected with an actual receiving example whose delay began at Chime's wrong queue sign. The sign had been corrected, but the cost question remained. Deng proposed retaining the location of the service failure beside its actual handling account. The representatives asked for a comparison of two verified cases before approving a rule. Nobody at the public bench could resolve the disputed allocation by applauding the fairest sounding speech.

lantern_03_029.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_029.text: Lower Glass had a different concern. Its receiving clerk had been paid for relay windows that rarely brought more than one packet. A carrier could combine those packets with a market route at lower cost, but would arrive later. The households using the window had not yet accepted that change. The representative offered a named consultation date and asked for the current sender count with private contents excluded. Deng agreed to prepare admitted counts. A low queue could make a service expensive without proving that its remaining users needed it less.

lantern_03_030.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_030.text: Moss Ford's delegate wanted the old relay preserved because her father had helped build its original stair. She said that plainly before offering her current cost questions. Jin Lu answered only the technical part. The stair's inspection and the isolation assembly's remaining life belonged to different records. Repairing the stair could keep an admitted viewing walk sound; it could not extend a failed joint. The delegate listened, looked angry at the device rather than at Jin, and asked for the actual retirement criteria on the public summary.

lantern_03_031.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_031.text: The representatives accepted the forty-five-day appropriation within its defined headings. They reserved a separate review of later service before this term ended. Fuel purchase, operator supplements, ground alternatives, and the proposed source appointment remained finite commitments. Deng signed the accepted minute after each authorised member checked the relevant figures. Yue could observe an institution choosing its own responsibilities. Her prior journeys had supplied questions she understood, but no vote. She left the hall before the private settlement staffing papers opened and took her public copy back to the lodging house.

lantern_03_032.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_032.text: On Day 1405 Bao's cheaper room remained unavailable while its occupant's repaired house dried. Its owner had taken no deposit and could not offer a false vacancy. Yue retained the quote, then renewed her existing room for six nights, Days 1406 through 1411, at two copper each. She paid twelve from money already held, including actual accepted merchant work. The higher charge was a real cost of waiting. Her cheaper proposal remained a possible later booking, not savings she could spend while somebody else still occupied the dry bed.

lantern_03_033.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_033.text: The setback annoyed her more than its modest size suggested. She had already pictured the saved copper becoming examination fees. In that picture, someone else's delayed home repair had vanished. Yue went outside and sat beside a public washing trough until her irritation grew less theatrical. A worker asked whether she wanted the next turn at the water. She did. Filling her own basin gave her hands a task which required neither good intentions nor an improved opinion of herself. She carried it inside before the next worker needed the space.

lantern_03_034.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_034.text: On Day 1405, Fen Tao's replacement sleeve passed the post-repair check within its admitted scope. Jin removed the stop tag for the affected afternoon window and kept the old joint's remaining-life notice visible. Ma reopened bookings for the current next window. Messages already handed to ground carriers were not pulled back into the lamp queue merely to make it look busy again. Their owners had chosen another paid route. Yue watched Ma reconcile the actual packet list, retaining the costs of changed choices rather than replacing them with a cleaner imagined schedule.

lantern_03_035.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_035.text: The apprenticeship sender received a ground-carrier arrival note that afternoon. Her son's message had reached the interview clerk, who would send the actual reply through his own office. Ma recorded only the admitted delivery reference. Yue knew no interview result and did not infer success from the woman's relieved expression. A real delivery could reduce uncertainty without deciding the matter inside its cover. The woman thanked the sign worker by name. He had moved the plank and now returned to repairing a stool for the same public bench.

lantern_03_036.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_036.text: Zheng visited the public viewing walk after his household appointment allowed it. He could see the replaced sleeve through the admitted inspection window and asked Jin a technical question. She answered the public part and offered the fuller record only under an appropriate qualified review. Zheng no longer held the association's examination post. He accepted that limit, though his fingers moved as if wanting the old tool. Yue asked whether he wanted to join a paid teaching proposal later. He wanted to read its dates first. Bao would have appreciated that answer.

lantern_03_037.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_037.text: A retired fitter still had useful knowledge. The current examiner still had to decide what was safe under her own appointment and actual records. Yue saw how easily affection for the old fitter could become pressure on the new examiner to permit a generous exception. Zheng himself interrupted a porter who wanted Jin to let him handle the assembly for old times' sake. He said old times had already supplied their own records. Today's equipment belonged to today's accepted workers. The porter looked surprised to hear the limit from the person he had tried to honour.

lantern_03_038.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_038.text: Deng's clerk returned the pending appointment dates on Day 1406. The proposed local term would begin after the presently accepted receiving timing was confirmed and would end eighteen calendar days later at the stated five-copper rate. Any basin correspondence occurring within it would retain its separate origin, hours, and receiving reference. The local duties needed no basin apparatus or unoffered household fields. Yue read the actual comparison with her own obligations, asked one question about correction letters arriving during rest, and waited for an answer before signing.

lantern_03_039.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_039.text: Deng answered that a rest-day delivery could wait in the named secure receiving tray until the next duty period unless its actual accepted terms required another authorised receiver. The association would appoint that receiver rather than demand Yue's constant availability. Her four-hour duty period covered local copying and comparison. Powered operation, qualified maintenance decisions, and every institution's unrelated mail remained outside it. Yue liked the offer better when its limits became specific enough that another person could tell whether a request exceeded them.

lantern_03_040.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_040.text: She accepted the local documentary appointment only under the clerk's confirmed compatible dates, retained her own signed copy, and asked for the first actual duty list. Deng gave her three public tasks: check the six receiving headings, compare admitted arrival and custody references, and prepare a correction circulation request from the food seller's offered location. The list had no hidden examination. Yue would remain at the stage her certificate described while working on it. The five-copper daily wages began under this accepted term, rather than at the moment she first wanted Chime to employ her.

lantern_03_041.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_041.text: Yue's first duty morning was Day 1407. The signed local term ran through Day 1424, eighteen calendar days at five copper, with the existing weekly rest and four-hour duty period. Its ninety copper remained committed wages until actual settlement under that term. The clerk retained the separate basin receiving timing beside it, making the compatibility review visible. Yue signed only the work she had accepted. She kept the lodging costs in her personal account because the local appointment had supplied no room by implication.

lantern_03_042.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_042.text: Ma gave her a public location list with six current receiving headings. One heading still used an older store name, though its public desk had moved next door. The store owner permitted the location correction. Yue walked the admitted public route with the assigned local messenger and measured its ordinary walking interval by the house clock. They did not inspect the owner's private storeroom. The corrected heading would guide senders to a desk, which was the actual purpose of the list.

lantern_03_043.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_043.text: The Lower Glass receiving clerk supplied a signed correction to her own contact hours. Her morning desk opened after the school meal delivery, a duty funded through a different account. Chime's old list had assumed she remained at the table through that interval. Yue placed the two timetables beside one another. Ma confirmed that relay arrival during the meal duty needed an assigned temporary custodian, rather than a notice asking the clerk to occupy two rooms. The settlement would appoint that person under its own staffing minute.

lantern_03_044.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_044.text: Yue drafted a request for the actual temporary custody arrangement. Deng returned it because the heading sounded as if Chime had already appointed somebody. Yue changed the heading to a request, preserving the named decision date. The correction cost ten minutes within her duty period. It did not become a moral injury to be repaired by staying late. At the end of four hours, she put the unfinished follow-up in the accepted queue, recorded its current status, and left the desk for the next paid worker.

lantern_03_045.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_045.text: Outside, a cloth seller offered to mend Yue's cloak hem for one copper. Bao could do the same work, but had accepted enough sewing for the week and had made no offer about this cloak. Yue paid the seller after agreeing the exact repair and collecting time. She would not turn acquaintance with Bao into an unasked cheaper service. The repaired hem stopped catching on the lodging door. It used money she could trace to her own work, without needing the association to pretend clothing belonged to its operating inventory.

lantern_03_046.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_046.text: On Day 1408, Ma received the food seller's current notice request from Yue's authorised duty file. The seller's stall lay on the association's actual contracted carrier route. Deng approved one public correction bundle for that stop from the existing circulation provision within the ground-alternative heading. Its printer and carrier would each receive their stated amount, with the bundle counted separately from private freight. The approval committed a specific delivery. It did not claim that every old advertisement wrapper would vanish from the market before another traveller ate there.

lantern_03_047.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_047.text: The bundle contained the current relay windows, the stopped-window alternatives, and the correction address. Yue checked the printed proof against Ma's admitted schedule. A printer had dropped the phrase subject to current route clearance from the ground-carrier line. The omission made the carrier sound able to travel through a closure. Yue restored it before the run, under the accepted copying task. The printer reissued the proof and retained the superseded one with its actual error mark. The paper correction used funded labour rather than hoping a careful reader would infer the missing condition.

lantern_03_048.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_048.text: Deng paid the approved printing amount against the actual accepted copies. The carrier signed the counted bundle before departure and left on his own scheduled route. Yue placed the dispatch receipt in the file and left delivery pending. The seller had requested useful information at an actual stall. This chain could meet that request if the ordinary carrier reached him. The lamp was not involved in transporting the bundle, and its reopened afternoon window did not supply a second imaginary delivery. A single request had one present dispatch and one receiver still ahead.

lantern_03_049.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_049.text: Rui came to the desk to return the school's two rejected samples before her home carriage. She did not ask the association to reverse its technical schedule for her departure. The sample owners' actual return instructions named their receiving shop, whose ordinary carrier route already served the school. She retained the price cards and paid the stated handling fee from the accepted purchasing account. Yue compared no private prices while copying the public receiver line Rui had offered for the local arrival example. The broader school transaction remained under school custody.

lantern_03_050.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_050.text: At midday, Jin Lu gave Deng the old assembly's updated remaining-life summary. It kept the current admitted windows and identified a final review before any further term could be offered. The replacement sleeve had addressed one wear point. Its receipt would not be used to certify the oldest joint as new. Deng asked whether retaining the lamp's exterior shell was safe if operation ended. Jin said its inert display needed a separate ordinary building and mounting check. A cold object and a working apparatus raised different questions, even when the public called both the lamp.

lantern_03_051.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_051.text: Yue wanted to know whether the shell's preservation could help Chime obtain more operating fuel. Deng answered that a display proposal bought no fuel contract. The current appropriation purchased specified external cells, with delivery and inspection before issue. A later funding request would need its own source and quantities. Jin would reject a cell whose compatibility failed the admitted cradle test, regardless of the public affection surrounding the lamp. Yue copied those statements into the public technical summary only after their authors approved the fields they had actually offered.

lantern_03_052.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_052.text: On Day 1401, Rui introduced Yue to the Seven Spool cloth cooperative's received proof-review order. Its three hundred eighty-four copper came from already collected merchant printing fees: two hundred fifty-eight for reviewing one hundred twenty-nine short sheets, one hundred eight for printing and paper, eighteen for dispatch. Each actually accepted sheet paid two copper. Yue accepted two-hour afternoon periods after any morning duties through Day 1445, apart from the agreed weekly rest dates. The work used the merchants' own admitted labels and quantities, with no basin files or association fuel involved. Morning desk duties remained separately received.

lantern_03_053.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_053.text: Two working afternoons produced twelve accepted sheets. Suan Li paid twelve copper on Day 1401 and twelve on Day 1403, after each checked six-sheet receipt. Days 1402 and 1409 were agreed rest dates without proofs added between errands. Sixteen later accepted sheets brought thirty-two copper on Day 1410, closing twenty-eight sheets at fifty-six actually received. Yue put the coins in her personal purse before the next booked room charge. Rui retained all her separate purchasing duties; this merchant order gave no customer ownership of Chime's association papers or basin originals.

lantern_03_054.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_054.text: Zheng had arranged one short private lesson for his colleague's grandson through the household receiving contact. Its actual accepted day was later in the month. Bao put it beside her own sewing appointments, leaving enough space for their shared meal preparation. Yue asked whether the lesson was part of Chime's public proposal. It was not. The child and household would pay the stated fee under Zheng's own ordinary work. A possible association demonstration remained unaccepted. The same lens could take part in different lawful tasks without merging their clocks or payments.

lantern_03_055.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_055.text: The cheaper owner confirmed an eighteen-night booking, Days 1412 through 1429, at one and a half copper nightly with weekly payment and no meals. The former occupant's actual departure had been received. Yue accepted the room and its permitted dry storage before her occupied nights began. She could place her pack there while completing the paid old booking. The lower rate applied to the new nights and refunded none already used. Continued lodging after this finite term would need an ordinary newly received renewal.

lantern_03_056.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_056.text: On Day 1410, Yue returned to the paid desk and received the Lower Glass temporary custody reply. The settlement had appointed its regular school aide to the short arrival interval, with an additional defined allowance under its own staffing minute. The aide had accepted the duty and supplied her signature. Chime could now name the actual temporary receiver rather than ask a busy clerk to remain in two rooms. Yue updated the contact list, preserving the dates and return conditions. The aide's school duties outside that interval remained with their appointed staff.

lantern_03_057.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_057.text: Ma tested the revised heading with a porter carrying an admitted sample packet. He followed the public sign to the proper desk and read the temporary receiver's current hours. He had helped prepare the old list and first wanted to rely on memory. Ma asked him to use the actual changed fields. He did, arriving at the right door. The test supplied one observed successful route under today's schedule. Yue recorded that limited result and retained the pending question about readers approaching from the opposite street, which this porter had not tested.

lantern_03_058.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_058.text: The food seller's signed bundle receipt arrived through the returning carrier before Yue's duty period ended. He had received the current sheets and placed one beside the meal board as requested. He retained the others for actual travellers who asked. His note mentioned the old printed wrappers still in use for food, making their status clear rather than claiming every old time had been withdrawn physically. Ma closed the specific delivery request. Yue could now describe its completed chain without enlarging the result into a correction accomplished in every market.

lantern_03_059.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_059.text: Deng called the source-record appointment's first short review at the ordinary table. Yue had checked receiving headings, compared actual temporary custody, and completed the admitted correction delivery. Some other cases remained pending under their own owners' permissions. Deng wanted a count of all six settlements' households reached by the new notice. The admitted records supplied receiving desks and one stall, not a complete household audience. Yue offered the actual receiving count instead. Deng accepted it and removed the larger phrase from her proposed public note before approval.

lantern_03_060.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_060.text: Jin brought the initial external fuel inventory to the same table for the next day's operating review. The cabinet count would need comparison with issued transmission windows, bench portions, returned compatible cells, and the purchases not yet received. Yue's documentary appointment admitted a public quantity summary after the licensed examiner approved it. It admitted no handling of charged cells. The closed cabinet remained under Jin's keys. Its exact count belonged to the upcoming actual check, while the present fuel-purchase line described a funded order rather than energy already in Chime.

lantern_03_061.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_061.text: Ma checked the duty list for the next operator shift. The appointed relief worker had accepted the covered interval under the regional base wage rota. Jin and Ma's additional supplements remained in the association's finite account. A scheduled rest would not be supplied by an unnamed helpful apprentice. Yue put the staffing receipt beside the public summary reference and then stopped at the end of her four-hour period. The next task had a receiver paid to perform it. Staying in the room would not make that person's accepted work hers.

lantern_03_062.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_062.text: As Yue walked to the cheaper room, she passed the tower's public rail. A child had drawn the lamp with twelve enormous rays reaching settlements never named in the charter. The child's teacher had labelled it an imaginative drawing. Yue admired the orange chalk without treating it as a service map. Above it, the real notice named six points and four currently admitted windows. The picture could keep its vast light. The institution had to keep the smaller promise it had actually made.

lantern_03_063.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_063.text: At the new room, Yue placed her pack on the assigned shelf and checked that the pendant wrapper remained dry. She checked her repaired cloak hem before folding it beside her own bag. Her own notebook now held a signed local appointment, actual receiving results, unresolved source limits, and the address of a qualified examiner she had yet to meet. Nothing there opened another pair of channels by itself. She washed her bowl and set it on the sill, leaving tomorrow's charged inventory under the people whose keys could actually open it.

lantern_03_064.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_064.text: The room's other tenant, a tinsmith named Pu An, asked whether Yue snored. She said nobody had complained recently. He said complaints usually arrived too late to improve a night. His own kettle lids occupied a shallow box beneath the bed. He showed her its sharp corner and moved it away from her walking space. Their first household agreement concerned a real toe rather than either person's profession. Yue placed her wrapped sword where its ordinary sheath could strike neither box nor sleeper.

lantern_03_065.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_065.text: Pu was making a little round lid for his daughter's toy pot from an offered scrap. He had missed her birthday while completing a paid roof order, and the household had celebrated without waiting for him. Yue asked whether he would take the lid home himself. His employer had approved a visiting afternoon later in the month. He could afford the journey if the last invoice was paid on its actual date. He wanted the visit, not another reason to ask his daughter to postpone being happy.

lantern_03_066.speaker: narrator
lantern_03_066.text: Yue left him to finish the rim and took her letter draft to the common table. She wrote that she had arrived, found work with specified hours, and taken a cheaper room after its earlier occupant could actually leave. She saved the unsent page until the next paid post collection.
